questions.stem: A constitution is best described as

options.text: the body of rules establishing the organs of government and regulating the relationship between government and the governed
the collection of all the laws passed by a legislature in a given year
the manifesto of the political party currently in power
a treaty between two or more sovereign states

questions.explanation: A constitution does three things: it creates the organs of government, it distributes power among them, and it defines the relationship between the state and the citizen. Because it is the supreme law, ordinary laws must conform to it.

distractorRationale.b: Ordinary legislation is subordinate to the constitution and is void where it conflicts with it
distractorRationale.c: A party manifesto is a statement of political intentions with no legal force
distractorRationale.d: An agreement between sovereign states is a treaty, which operates in international rather than constitutional law

questions.stem: Which country is the classic example of a state with an unwritten constitution?

options.text: The United States of America
The United Kingdom
Nigeria
India

questions.explanation: Britain's constitutional rules are found in scattered statutes, judicial decisions, conventions and historical documents rather than in one codified enactment. This does not mean Britain lacks a constitution; it means the constitution has never been assembled into a single document.

distractorRationale.a: The American constitution of 1787 is the oldest written constitution still in force
distractorRationale.c: Nigeria's constitution is codified in a single document, most recently that of 1999
distractorRationale.d: India has a written constitution, adopted in 1949 and in force from 1950

questions.stem: A rigid constitution is one which

options.text: can never be amended under any circumstances
can be amended only by a special and difficult procedure
is contained in a single written document
may be amended by the ordinary law-making process

questions.explanation: Rigidity is about the amendment procedure, not about impossibility. A rigid constitution demands something extra — a special majority, the consent of component states, or a referendum — so that it cannot be altered by a passing legislative majority.

distractorRationale.a: No constitution is unamendable; rigidity makes amendment difficult, not impossible
distractorRationale.c: Being in one document makes a constitution written, which is a separate classification
distractorRationale.d: Amendment by the ordinary law-making process describes a flexible constitution

questions.stem: Under section 9 of the 1999 Constitution of Nigeria, an ordinary constitutional amendment requires the support of

options.text: a simple majority of members present and voting in the Senate only
two-thirds of all the members of each House of the National Assembly and approval by two-thirds of the State Houses of Assembly
a national referendum in which a majority of registered voters take part
the President acting alone by executive order

questions.explanation: Section 9 sets a double hurdle: a two-thirds majority of all members in each chamber of the National Assembly, and then approval by resolution of the Houses of Assembly of not less than two-thirds of all the states. Requiring the states to agree is what makes the amendment procedure genuinely federal as well as rigid.

distractorRationale.a: A simple majority in one chamber is the standard for ordinary legislation, not for constitutional amendment
distractorRationale.c: Nigeria's constitution does not provide for a referendum as the route to amendment, unlike some other countries
distractorRationale.d: Amending the constitution by executive order would destroy the supremacy of the constitution over the executive

sources.title: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999, section 9

questions.stem: Which THREE of the following are recognised sources of a constitution?

options.text: Judicial precedents interpreting the rules of government
Conventions and long-observed political customs
Opinion polls conducted during an election campaign
Historical documents and charters such as the Magna Carta
Editorials published in privately owned newspapers

questions.explanation: Decided cases settle what the constitutional rules mean, conventions supply binding practices that were never written down, and historical charters record the original bargains between rulers and ruled. All three genuinely shape the rules by which a state is governed.

distractorRationale.c: Opinion polls measure passing public mood and create no binding rule of government
distractorRationale.e: Newspaper editorials may influence debate but they carry no constitutional authority

questions.stem: Why is a written constitution considered especially necessary in a federal state?

options.text: Because it can set out precisely the powers of the central and state governments
Because it makes the central government stronger than the states
Because it removes the need for courts to interpret the law
Because federal states always have larger populations

questions.explanation: Federalism only works if each tier knows exactly what it may and may not do. Nigeria's Second Schedule does this through the Exclusive and Concurrent Legislative Lists, leaving residual matters to the states. Without a written division of powers, disputes between the tiers could not be settled.

distractorRationale.b: A written constitution defines and limits central power rather than automatically enlarging it
distractorRationale.c: A written constitution increases the courts' interpretive role, since disputes are argued over its wording
distractorRationale.d: Population size has nothing to do with the need to codify a division of powers

sources.title: Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999, Second Schedule

questions.stem: Every written constitution is necessarily a rigid constitution.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: False. Whether a constitution is written depends on codification into one document; whether it is rigid depends on how hard it is to amend. A written constitution that could be amended by an ordinary Act of the legislature would be written but flexible, so the two classifications must be kept apart.

distractorRationale.a: Nigeria happens to be both written and rigid, which tempts students to treat the two labels as one and the same

questions.stem: State three merits and two demerits of a written constitution.
markingGuide: Merit: it is clear and precise, so citizens, officials and courts can consult and cite it, reducing disputes about what the rules are (2 marks)
Merit: it is suitable for a federation because it can define the powers of the central and state governments, as Nigeria's legislative lists do (2 marks)
Merit: it entrenches citizens' fundamental rights in a form the courts can enforce, and cannot easily be manipulated by rulers (2 marks)
Demerit: it tends to be rigid and slow to adapt, so reform may be blocked even when circumstances have plainly changed (2 marks)
Demerit: no document can foresee every situation, so much depends on judicial interpretation, which transfers considerable power to unelected judges (2 marks)
questions.explanation: The merits cluster around certainty, enforceability and the protection of rights and of the federal bargain. The demerits cluster around inflexibility and dependence on interpretation. A strong answer illustrates at least one point with a Nigerian example, such as section 9's amendment hurdles as evidence of rigidity.
